# Findings reference

<!-- Generated by tools/New-FindingDocs.ps1 - do not edit by hand. -->

Every problem the script reports has a stable **finding ID**. This page explains what each one means and what to do about it. The severity shown is the default; some findings change their severity depending on the evidence.

Total: **147** findings. IDs ending in a dash-placeholder (for example `disk-health-<id>`) exist once per drive, adapter or event source.

## Accounts

<a id="accounts-nopw"></a>
### `accounts-nopw`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … account(s) do not require a password

**What it means.** Anyone with access to the PC (or the network, if file sharing/RDP is on) can sign in without a password.

**What to do.** Set a password (or a PIN with Windows Hello) for these accounts.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"accounts-nopw"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="guest-enabled"></a>
### `guest-enabled`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** The Guest account is enabled

**What it means.** The Guest account allows sign-in without a personal account and is rarely needed.

**What to do.** net user Guest /active:no (admin prompt).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"guest-enabled"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="many-admins"></a>
### `many-admins`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** … accounts have administrator rights

**What it means.** The more administrator accounts, the bigger the attack surface.

**What to do.** Remove administrator rights from accounts that do not need them (Settings > Accounts > Family & other users).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"many-admins"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="no-lockout"></a>
### `no-lockout`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Accounts are never locked after failed sign-ins

**What it means.** Without an account lockout threshold, passwords can be guessed indefinitely (relevant if RDP or file sharing is reachable).

**What to do.** Local Security Policy > Account Policies > Account Lockout Policy: threshold 10, duration 15 minutes.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"no-lockout"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="stale-accounts"></a>
### `stale-accounts`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** … enabled account(s) not used for 6+ months

**What it means.** Forgotten accounts are easy targets because nobody notices misuse.

**What to do.** Disable or delete accounts you no longer need (Settings > Accounts > Family & other users).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"stale-accounts"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="builtin-admin"></a>
### `builtin-admin`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** The built-in Administrator account (…) is enabled

**What it means.** This well-known account name is the first target of password guessing and has no UAC prompt protection by default.

**What to do.** Use a normal account that is a member of Administrators and disable the built-in one unless you need it.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"builtin-admin"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Apps

<a id="store-app-error"></a>
### `store-app-error`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** … Store app(s) could not be updated

**What it means.** An app could not be updated, e.g. because it is currently running or the Store cache is corrupted.

**What to do.** Close the apps and run again; if that does not help, open "Downloads and updates" in the Store or run "wsreset.exe" (only resets the Store cache).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"store-app-error"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="store-check"></a>
### `store-check`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** Please check the Store updates once in the Store

**What it means.** There is no official interface with which a script can reliably confirm that all Store apps are really up to date.

**What to do.** Open Microsoft Store > 'Library' (or 'Downloads and updates') > 'Get updates'.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"store-check"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="store-missing"></a>
### `store-missing`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** The Microsoft Store is not installed

**What it means.** Some editions (e.g. LTSC) have no Store, or it was removed. In that case there are no Store app updates either.

**What to do.** If it should be there: PowerShell (admin) 'Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers Microsoft.WindowsStore | ForEach-Object { Add-AppxPackage -DisableDevelopmentMode -Register "…\AppxManifest.xml" }'.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"store-missing"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="winget-desktop-updates"></a>
### `winget-desktop-updates`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** … desktop app(s) can be updated via winget

**What it means.** Outdated browsers, archivers and media players are a common way for malware to get in.

**What to do.** Run 'winget upgrade' in a terminal to list them, then 'winget upgrade --all' to update.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"winget-desktop-updates"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Disks

<a id="disk-health"></a>
### `disk-health-<…>`

**Severity:** Critical · **Title:** Disk reports a health problem: …

**What it means.** Windows rates this disk as unhealthy (warning or error). The hard drive/SSD may fail soon; data may be lost.

**What to do.** Make a complete backup IMMEDIATELY. Then run the manufacturer's diagnostic tool and replace the drive if confirmed.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"disk-health*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="smart-fail"></a>
### `smart-fail`

**Severity:** Critical · **Title:** SMART predicts an imminent failure of a drive

**What it means.** SMART is the self-monitoring of hard drives/SSDs. The warning means: the drive expects to fail soon.

**What to do.** Make a backup immediately and replace the drive.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"smart-fail"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="dirty-bit"></a>
### `dirty-bit`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** The system drive is flagged 'dirty'

**What it means.** Windows marked the file system as possibly inconsistent (after a crash/power loss). A disk check will run at the next restart.

**What to do.** Restart and let the check finish; run the Integrity module afterwards.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"dirty-bit"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="disk-readerr"></a>
### `disk-readerr-<…>`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** Uncorrectable read errors: …

**What it means.** The disk could not read data without errors. This is an early warning sign of data loss.

**What to do.** Make a backup, check the drive with the manufacturer's tool.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"disk-readerr*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="disk-wear"></a>
### `disk-wear-<…>`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** SSD is heavily worn (… % wear): …

**What it means.** SSDs only tolerate a limited amount of write operations. With high wear the probability of failure increases.

**What to do.** Make a backup and plan a replacement.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"disk-wear*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="disk-writeerr"></a>
### `disk-writeerr-<…>`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** Uncorrectable write errors: …

**What it means.** The disk could not write data without errors. The drive or its connection is failing.

**What to do.** Make a backup immediately and replace the drive.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"disk-writeerr*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="space"></a>
### `space-<…>`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** System drive almost full: only … free

**What it means.** Windows needs free space for updates, the page file and temporary files. With less than about 10 GB, updates fail and the PC becomes slow.

**What to do.** Check large files/programs (Settings > System > Storage), clean up downloads, move data to another drive if necessary.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"space*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="vol-health"></a>
### `vol-health-<…>`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** File system of …: reports problems

**What it means.** The file system is marked as unhealthy (errors or check pending).

**What to do.** Run the 'Integrity and repair' module (file system check) or in Explorer: drive > Properties > Tools > Check.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"vol-health*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="disk-temp"></a>
### `disk-temp-<…>`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** Disk is hot (… °C): …

**What it means.** Permanently high temperatures shorten the lifespan and can lead to throttling.

**What to do.** Check case ventilation/dust, retrofit a heat sink for M.2 SSDs if necessary.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"disk-temp*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Drivers

<a id="driver-problems"></a>
### `driver-problems`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … device(s) with an error in Device Manager

**What it means.** A driver is missing for these devices or the driver does not work. The device (e.g. WLAN, sound card, card reader) then does not work or only works in a limited way.

**What to do.** Let Windows Update look for drivers (optional updates) or download the driver from the manufacturer of the device or laptop. Device Manager > right-click the device > Update driver.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"driver-problems"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="drivers-unsigned"></a>
### `drivers-unsigned`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … unsigned driver(s) installed

**What it means.** Unsigned kernel drivers were not verified by Microsoft. They are a stability risk and a favourite hiding place for rootkits.

**What to do.** Update the drivers from the manufacturer, or uninstall the device/software if you do not recognise it.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"drivers-unsigned"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="gpu-driver"></a>
### `gpu-driver-<…>`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** Graphics driver is over 2 years old (…)

**What it means.** Current graphics drivers fix crashes, display glitches and security holes, and often bring performance in games. Windows Update usually only delivers older versions.

**What to do.** Get the current driver directly from the manufacturer (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel). For security reasons the script does not install drivers from third-party sites.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"gpu-driver*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Event log

<a id="evt"></a>
### `evt-<…>`

**Severity:** $kb.S · **Title:** … - …x in 7 days

**What it means.** …

**What to do.** …

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"evt*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="evt-appcrash"></a>
### `evt-appcrash`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** Programs crash repeatedly

**What it means.** A program is terminated by Windows because of a severe error. Repeated crashes of the same program point to a broken installation, incompatibility, outdated version or faulty drivers/hardware.

**What to do.** Update or reinstall the affected program. If many different programs crash, check the RAM (mdsched.exe) and disks.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"evt-appcrash"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="evtlog-cleared"></a>
### `evtlog-cleared`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** An event log was cleared in the last 30 days

**What it means.** Clearing logs removes evidence. You may have done it with a "cleaner" tool; if not, it is a typical step after a compromise.

**What to do.** If you did not do this, run a full offline Defender scan and change important passwords.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"evtlog-cleared"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="evtlog-off"></a>
### `evtlog-off-<…>`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** The event log '…' is disabled

**What it means.** Without it Windows and the script cannot see errors or Defender detections.

**What to do.** Enable the log in Event Viewer (right-click > Enable Log).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"evtlog-off*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="evt-apphang"></a>
### `evt-apphang`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Programs repeatedly stop responding

**What it means.** Programs that stop responding ("Not responding") point to overload, a slow disk or software errors.

**What to do.** Update/reinstall the program, watch disk health and RAM usage.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"evt-apphang"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="evt-other"></a>
### `evt-other`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** … other error message(s) occur frequently

**What it means.** The script does not know these messages in detail. Individual errors in the event log are normal for Windows; what matters are accumulations or messages that match noticeable problems.

**What to do.** Search online for "<source> event <ID>". Only intervene if you also notice problems.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"evt-other"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Hardware

<a id="memdiag-errors"></a>
### `memdiag-errors`

**Severity:** Critical · **Title:** Windows Memory Diagnostic found RAM errors

**What it means.** The memory test reported errors. Defective RAM causes blue screens, corrupted files and random crashes.

**What to do.** Test one RAM stick at a time (MemTest86), remove or replace the faulty module. Undo XMP/overclocking first.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"memdiag-errors"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="temp-high"></a>
### `temp-high`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** A thermal sensor reports … °C

**What it means.** Sustained temperatures this high cause throttling, crashes and shorten component life.

**What to do.** Clean dust from fans and vents, check the fans spin, replace dried thermal paste, use the PC on a hard surface.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"temp-high"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="battery-weak"></a>
### `battery-weak`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Battery has only … % of its original capacity

**What it means.** Lithium batteries wear out. Below 60 % the device lasts much shorter and, in extreme cases, the battery can swell.

**What to do.** Have the battery replaced. If the case is bulging, disconnect the device from power immediately.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"battery-weak"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="bios-old"></a>
### `bios-old`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** BIOS/UEFI is older than 5 years

**What it means.** The BIOS/UEFI is the firmware of the mainboard. Manufacturers fix stability and security problems in it. An update is not without risk, though, and only makes sense for specific problems.

**What to do.** Look for a BIOS update on the support page of the PC/mainboard manufacturer and follow the instructions exactly (make sure the power supply is stable!). Only necessary if you have problems.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"bios-old"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Integrity

<a id="dism-irreparable"></a>
### `dism-irreparable`

**Severity:** Critical · **Title:** The Windows component store is not repairable

**What it means.** Windows can no longer repair its own system components by itself. Updates and system functions become increasingly unreliable.

**What to do.** Recommended: 'repair upgrade' - start the setup file with the Windows 10 Media Creation Tool (microsoft.com/software-download/windows10) and choose 'Keep personal files and apps'. This reinstalls Windows 10 but keeps your data. Make a backup BEFOREHAND.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"dism-irreparable"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="dism-broken"></a>
### `dism-broken`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** The Windows component store is damaged (repairable)

**What it means.** The component store (WinSxS) is the "spare parts depot" of Windows. Damage leads to failing updates, errors in Windows features and instability.

**What to do.** A repair will be attempted (DISM RestoreHealth).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"dism-broken"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="sfc-unrepairable"></a>
### `sfc-unrepairable`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** SFC finds corrupted system files that cannot be repaired

**What it means.** Windows system files are corrupted and the automatic repair failed. This shows up as crashes, failing updates or missing features.

**What to do.** 1) Restart, run the script again. 2) If that does not help: repair upgrade with the Windows 10 Media Creation Tool (option 'Keep personal files and apps'). Details: C:\Windows\Logs\CBS\CBS.log (search for '[SR]').

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"sfc-unrepairable"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="sfc-violations"></a>
### `sfc-violations`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** SFC finds corrupted system files (DryRun: not repaired)

**What it means.** The read-only check found damaged Windows system files.

**What to do.** Run the script without -DryRun to repair them (DISM + SFC).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"sfc-violations"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="wmi-broken"></a>
### `wmi-broken`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** WMI repository is inconsistent

**What it means.** WMI is the database from which Windows and many programs query system information. If it is damaged, hardware info, diagnostic tools and sometimes updates fail.

**What to do.** A repair will be attempted (winmgmt /salvagerepository).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"wmi-broken"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="dism-error"></a>
### `dism-error`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** DISM could not check/repair the component store

**What it means.** DISM is the repair tool for the component store. …

**What to do.** Restart and try again. Log: C:\Windows\Logs\DISM\dism.log. If that does not help, perform a repair upgrade with the Media Creation Tool.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"dism-error"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="sfc-not-run"></a>
### `sfc-not-run`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** SFC could not be run

**What it means.** The system file check was aborted by Windows - often because a restart is pending or the Windows Modules Installer (TrustedInstaller) does not start.

**What to do.** Restart Windows and run the script again.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"sfc-not-run"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="sfc-repaired"></a>
### `sfc-repaired`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** Corrupted system files were repaired

**What it means.** SFC found modified or corrupted Windows system files and replaced them with originals. Corruption results from crashes, power outages, disk errors, faulty tuning tools or malware.

**What to do.** The script fixed this automatically. If such findings occur repeatedly, check disk health and RAM.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"sfc-repaired"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="sfc-timeout"></a>
### `sfc-timeout`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** SFC took too long and was stopped

**What it means.** The system file check did not finish within 90 minutes. This is unusual and often points to a very slow or failing disk.

**What to do.** Check disk health (SMART section of this report), restart and run the script again.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"sfc-timeout"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="sfc-unclear"></a>
### `sfc-unclear`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** SFC result unclear

**What it means.** The script could not derive a clear result from the console and the CBS log.

**What to do.** Open the CBS log (C:\Windows\Logs\CBS\CBS.log) and search for '[SR]', or run 'sfc /verifyonly' manually.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"sfc-unclear"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Network

<a id="dns-error"></a>
### `dns-error`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** Internet reachable, but name resolution (DNS) does not work

**What it means.** DNS translates web addresses into IP addresses. Without DNS, no browser, no Windows Update and no Store works even though the line is up.

**What to do.** Restart the router; alternatively enter a different DNS server in the adapter settings (e.g. 1.1.1.1 or 9.9.9.9).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"dns-error"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="offline"></a>
### `offline`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** No internet connection

**What it means.** Without internet, Windows Update, the Store, Defender updates and DISM repairs from the web are not possible.

**What to do.** Check cable/WLAN, router and airplane mode. Then start the script again. If Windows network problems persist: Settings > Network & Internet > Network troubleshooter.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"offline"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="ports-risky"></a>
### `ports-risky`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** Unencrypted remote-access services are listening on the network

**What it means.** Telnet, FTP and VNC without tunnel send passwords in clear text and are frequently attacked.

**What to do.** Stop and disable the service, or block the port in Windows Firewall.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"ports-risky"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="gateway-bad"></a>
### `gateway-bad`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** Connection to the router is unstable

**What it means.** Packet loss or high latency to the router itself (not the internet) points to Wi-Fi/cable problems in your local network.

**What to do.** Check cable/Wi-Fi, restart the router, update the network driver.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"gateway-bad"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="shares-everyone"></a>
### `shares-everyone`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … network share(s) are open to Everyone

**What it means.** Anyone who can reach this PC on the network can read (or change) the shared folder.

**What to do.** Share only with named users (folder > Properties > Sharing > Advanced Sharing > Permissions) or remove the share.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"shares-everyone"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="user-proxy"></a>
### `user-proxy`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** A browser/system proxy is configured for your user

**What it means.** All web traffic of Chrome, Edge and many programs goes through this proxy. In companies this is normal; at home it is a typical result of adware or malware ("proxy hijack").

**What to do.** Settings > Network & Internet > Proxy: turn off "Use a proxy server" and "Use setup script" if you did not set them.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"user-proxy"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="link100"></a>
### `link100-<…>`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Ethernet adapter '…' links at only 100 Mbps

**What it means.** Modern gigabit hardware falling back to 100 Mbps usually means a damaged cable, a bad port or a very old switch.

**What to do.** Try another cable (Cat5e or better) and another switch/router port.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"link100*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="metered"></a>
### `metered`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** The active connection is set to "metered"

**What it means.** On a metered connection Windows postpones most update downloads. Updates can look "stuck" even though nothing is wrong.

**What to do.** Settings > Network & Internet > (your connection) > Properties > "Set as metered connection": Off (unless you really have a data cap).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"metered"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="neterr"></a>
### `neterr-<…>`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Adapter '…' shows many packet errors/discards

**What it means.** Frequent packet errors point to a bad cable, interference or a driver problem.

**What to do.** Replace the cable, update the network driver, check for Wi-Fi interference.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"neterr*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="wifi-weak"></a>
### `wifi-weak`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Weak Wi-Fi signal (… %)

**What it means.** A weak signal causes slow speeds, drops and failed downloads (including updates).

**What to do.** Move closer to the router, use the 5 GHz band, or add a mesh/access point.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"wifi-weak"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="ports-info"></a>
### `ports-info`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** File sharing / remote management ports are open

**What it means.** These ports are normal for file sharing or remote administration but should never be reachable from the internet.

**What to do.** On a home PC without sharing: turn off file sharing (Network and Sharing Center) and Remote Desktop.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"ports-info"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="winhttp-proxy"></a>
### `winhttp-proxy`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** A system-wide WinHTTP proxy is set

**What it means.** Windows Update and the Store use this proxy. In company networks this is normal; on a home network a forgotten proxy often prevents updates (error 0x8024402C).

**What to do.** If no proxy is wanted: PowerShell (admin) 'netsh winhttp reset proxy'.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"winhttp-proxy"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Performance

<a id="cpu-throttle"></a>
### `cpu-throttle`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** CPU runs at only … % of its clock speed under load

**What it means.** The processor is busy but not boosting. Typical causes: overheating, a weak power plan ("Power saver"), a failing fan or dust in the heat sink, or power limits set by the laptop.

**What to do.** Check the power plan, clean fans and vents, check temperatures (e.g. HWiNFO).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"cpu-throttle"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="disk-busy"></a>
### `disk-busy`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** The system drive is busy (…) % active)

**What it means.** A constantly busy drive makes the whole PC feel slow. Typical culprits: indexing, antivirus scans, updates, an almost full or failing disk (especially an HDD).

**What to do.** Wait for background work to finish, check disk health in this report, and consider an SSD if this is a hard disk.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"disk-busy"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="ram-full"></a>
### `ram-full`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** Memory is … % used

**What it means.** When memory is almost full, Windows moves data to the (slower) disk and the PC becomes noticeably slow.

**What to do.** Look for memory-hungry programs in Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc), trim the autostart items or install more RAM.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"ram-full"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="boot-slow"></a>
### `boot-slow`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Windows takes about … seconds to start

**What it means.** A start longer than two minutes usually means too many startup programs, a slow or full drive, or a driver that delays the boot.

**What to do.** See the list of slow startup items in this report, reduce autostart programs and check disk health.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"boot-slow"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="pagefile-manual"></a>
### `pagefile-manual`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** The page file is not managed automatically

**What it means.** A fixed page file that is set too small can lead to memory errors and crashes; otherwise Windows can adjust the size optimally by itself.

**What to do.** Enable automatic management (System Properties > Advanced > Performance > Settings > Advanced > Virtual memory).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"pagefile-manual"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="powerplan-saver"></a>
### `powerplan-saver`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** A desktop PC runs on the "Power saver" plan

**What it means.** Power saver limits the CPU speed. On a desktop this just makes the PC slower without saving noticeable energy.

**What to do.** Control Panel > Power Options > choose 'Balanced'.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"powerplan-saver"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="shutdown-slow"></a>
### `shutdown-slow`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** … slow shutdowns in 30 days

**What it means.** Windows had to wait for an app or service to close during shutdown.

**What to do.** Update or uninstall the programs named in Event Viewer > Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > Diagnostics-Performance (event 203).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"shutdown-slow"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="startup-many"></a>
### `startup-many`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** … programs start automatically with Windows

**What it means.** Every startup program prolongs system start and occupies memory. Many of them (updaters, helper programs, launchers) are not needed all the time.

**What to do.** Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) > "Startup" tab: set programs with "High impact" that you do not need all the time to "Disabled". The script deliberately does not do this itself, because only you know what you need. The list is in the appendix of the report.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"startup-many"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="fast-startup"></a>
### `fast-startup`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** Fast Startup is turned on

**What it means.** Fast Startup saves the system state on 'Shut down' and therefore starts faster. Downside: there is no real restart, driver and update problems survive the 'Shut down'.

**What to do.** The script does not change this. For strange errors use 'Restart' instead of 'Shut down' or turn off Fast Startup under Control Panel > Power Options > 'Choose what the power buttons do'.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"fast-startup"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="ram-low"></a>
### `ram-low`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** Little memory installed (… GB)

**What it means.** With less than 8 GB of RAM, modern software (browsers with many tabs, Office, video conferences) quickly becomes sluggish.

**What to do.** A RAM upgrade to 8-16 GB is often the most effective and cheapest speed-up, provided the device is expandable.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"ram-low"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="ram-single-channel"></a>
### `ram-single-channel`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** Only one RAM module installed (single channel)

**What it means.** Two identical modules run in dual-channel mode, which roughly doubles memory bandwidth. Integrated graphics and games benefit the most.

**What to do.** If the board has a free slot, add a second identical module.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"ram-single-channel"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="ram-slow"></a>
### `ram-slow`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** RAM runs slower than its rated speed

**What it means.** The modules are rated for a higher speed than they currently run at. Often XMP/DOCP is simply not enabled in the BIOS.

**What to do.** Enable XMP/DOCP in the BIOS/UEFI (stability test afterwards).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"ram-slow"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Persistence

<a id="wmi-persist"></a>
### `wmi-persist`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** … permanent WMI event subscription(s) found

**What it means.** WMI subscriptions can run programs invisibly at boot or on events. Almost no consumer software uses them, but fileless malware does.

**What to do.** Inspect with Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\subscription -ClassName __EventConsumer / __FilterToConsumerBinding, remove unknown ones and run a full offline scan.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"wmi-persist"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="run-suspicious"></a>
### `run-suspicious`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … autostart entr(ies) look unusual

**What it means.** Autostart entries that start scripts or run from Temp/AppData/Downloads are a common malware pattern.

**What to do.** Task Manager > Startup: disable what you do not recognise, then run a full scan.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"run-suspicious"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="svc-unquoted"></a>
### `svc-unquoted`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … service(s) have an unquoted path with spaces

**What it means.** If the path to a service is not in quotes, a local attacker can place a program such as "C:\Program.exe" that will be run as SYSTEM (privilege escalation).

**What to do.** Reinstall/update the software; or put the full path to the service in quotes under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<name>\ImagePath.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"svc-unquoted"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="svc-userpath"></a>
### `svc-userpath`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … service(s) run programs from user-writable folders

**What it means.** Services normally live in Program Files or Windows. A service started from a user profile or Temp folder is unusual and is a malware pattern.

**What to do.** Check what these services are; remove them if unknown and run a full scan.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"svc-userpath"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="tasks-suspicious"></a>
### `tasks-suspicious`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … scheduled task(s) look unusual

**What it means.** These tasks run from user-writable folders or use script/encoded-command tricks. Legitimate software does this sometimes, malware does it almost always.

**What to do.** Open Task Scheduler, check each task. If you do not recognise it, disable it, delete the file it starts and run a full virus scan.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"tasks-suspicious"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="run-unsigned"></a>
### `run-unsigned`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** … autostart program(s) have no valid digital signature

**What it means.** Unsigned does not mean malicious (many small tools are unsigned), but malware is almost never signed.

**What to do.** Check that you know each program; search its file name online if unsure.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"run-unsigned"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="svc-orphaned"></a>
### `svc-orphaned`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** … service(s) point to files that no longer exist

**What it means.** Remnants of removed software (or of malware that was cleaned up). Harmless but they log errors at every boot.

**What to do.** Admin prompt: sc delete <name> (after confirming the software is gone).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"svc-orphaned"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="tasks-orphaned"></a>
### `tasks-orphaned`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** … scheduled task(s) point to programs that no longer exist

**What it means.** Leftovers of uninstalled software. They fail silently at every trigger and clutter the system; malware cleanup also often leaves them.

**What to do.** Task Scheduler: delete these tasks.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"tasks-orphaned"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Recovery

<a id="bcd-error"></a>
### `bcd-error`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** The boot configuration (BCD) cannot be read

**What it means.** The boot configuration store is damaged or inaccessible. The PC may fail to boot after the next restart.

**What to do.** Boot from Windows installation media > Repair your computer > Command Prompt: bootrec /rebuildbcd. The script never does this automatically.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"bcd-error"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="bitlocker-nokey"></a>
### `bitlocker-nokey-<…>`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** BitLocker on … has no recovery password

**What it means.** If the TPM or hardware changes you can be locked out of your own data.

**What to do.** manage-bde -protectors -add … -RecoveryPassword, then store the key outside this PC.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"bitlocker-nokey*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="no-backup"></a>
### `no-backup`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** No Windows backup mechanism is in use

**What it means.** Neither File History, OneDrive folder backup nor a recent restore point was found. If the drive fails or ransomware hits, personal files are lost. (Third-party backup tools are not detected by this check.)

**What to do.** Turn on File History (Settings > Update & Security > Backup) or OneDrive "Back up" for Desktop/Documents/Pictures, and keep one copy offline.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"no-backup"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="winre-off"></a>
### `winre-off`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** The Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) is disabled

**What it means.** WinRE provides "Reset this PC", Startup Repair and System Restore from the boot menu. Without it a PC that no longer boots is much harder to rescue.

**What to do.** Admin prompt: 'reagentc /enable'. If that fails, the recovery partition is missing or too small.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"winre-off"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Script

<a id="module"></a>
### `module-<…>`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Module '…' was not fully executed

**What it means.** An unexpected error occurred in one step of the script. The remaining modules were run anyway. This is usually a sign of a blocked or broken Windows component.

**What to do.** Run the script again. If the error recurs, research the error text together with the console log (path at the end of the report).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"module*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="script-update"></a>
### `script-update`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** Version … of this script is available

**What it means.** A newer release exists on GitHub. The script never updates itself.

**What to do.** Review the release notes at …

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"script-update"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Security

<a id="autologon"></a>
### `autologon`

**Severity:** $(if ($hasPw) { 'High' } else { 'Low' }) · **Title:** Automatic sign-in is configured

**What it means.** Windows signs in without asking for a password. … { 'The password is stored in clear text in the registry (DefaultPassword) and readable by every administrator/process with registry access.' })

**What to do.** Run netplwiz and tick "Users must enter a user name and password", and delete the DefaultPassword value.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"autologon"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="defender-exclusions"></a>
### `defender-exclusions`

**Severity:** $(if ($risky.Count -gt 0) { 'Medium' } else { 'Info' }) · **Title:** Defender has … exclusion(s)

**What it means.** Files and folders on the exclusion list are never scanned. Malware often adds itself there; legitimate software (games, developer tools) sometimes does too.

**What to do.** Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage settings > Exclusions: remove everything you do not recognise.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"defender-exclusions"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="svc-running"></a>
### `svc-running-<…>`

**Severity:** $s.Sev · **Title:** … service is running

**What it means.** This service lets other computers query or reach this PC. Most home users never need it.

**What to do.** Stop-Service …; Set-Service … -StartupType Disabled (only if nothing you use depends on it).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"svc-running*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="defender-threat"></a>
### `defender-threat`

**Severity:** Critical · **Title:** Active threat(s) reported by Defender

**What it means.** Defender detected malware that has not been completely removed yet.

**What to do.** Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection history, apply the actions, then run a full scan (or offline scan) and change the passwords of important accounts.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"defender-threat"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="appinit"></a>
### `appinit`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** AppInit_DLLs is active

**What it means.** Every program that uses a window loads these DLLs. This old mechanism is used by malware and badly behaved "overlay" tools.

**What to do.** Remove the entry unless you know the software that needs it; run a full virus scan.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"appinit"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="defender-off"></a>
### `defender-off`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** Real-time antivirus protection is turned off

**What it means.** Without real-time protection, malware is not detected when opened/downloaded, and no other antivirus is active.

**What to do.** Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > turn on real-time protection.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"defender-off"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="dep-off"></a>
### `dep-off`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** Data Execution Prevention (DEP) is off system-wide

**What it means.** DEP blocks code from running in data memory, a basic defence against many exploits.

**What to do.** Windows Security > App & browser control > Exploit protection settings > DEP: Use default (On).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"dep-off"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="hosts-suspicious"></a>
### `hosts-suspicious`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** The hosts file blocks/redirects addresses of Microsoft or security vendors

**What it means.** The hosts file overrides DNS resolution. Entries for update or antivirus servers are a typical sign of malware (or of manual "telemetry blockers" - but then they also block updates).

**What to do.** Open the file C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts as admin in an editor and remove unknown entries, then run a full virus scan.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"hosts-suspicious"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="ifeo"></a>
### `ifeo`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** Programs are hijacked through Image File Execution Options

**What it means.** A "Debugger" value makes Windows start a different program whenever the named program (e.g. sethc.exe, utilman.exe, taskmgr.exe, an antivirus) is launched. This is a standard malware trick.

**What to do.** Delete the Debugger value (or key) after checking what it points to, then run a full virus scan.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"ifeo"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="no-av"></a>
### `no-av`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** No antivirus detected

**What it means.** Neither Microsoft Defender nor any other antivirus responds. The system is unprotected against malware.

**What to do.** Open Windows Security and enable Defender (or install a reputable antivirus).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"no-av"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="os-end-of-support"></a>
### `os-end-of-support`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** Windows 10 is (largely) out of support

**What it means.** …

**What to do.** Check security updates (see update section), use a current browser and antivirus, do not use the PC for risky activities, make backups. Long term: switch to a supported system (you explicitly excluded Windows 11 - an alternative is e.g. a Linux system) or secured operation with ESU.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"os-end-of-support"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="rdp-no-nla"></a>
### `rdp-no-nla`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** Remote Desktop does not require Network Level Authentication

**What it means.** Without NLA the login screen is exposed before authentication, which enables brute force and several known RDP exploits.

**What to do.** Settings > System > Remote Desktop > Advanced settings: require Network Level Authentication.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"rdp-no-nla"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="uac-off"></a>
### `uac-off`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** User Account Control (UAC) is turned off

**What it means.** UAC asks for confirmation before programs use administrator rights. When turned off, malware can dig deeper into the system unnoticed.

**What to do.** Control Panel > User Accounts > 'Change User Account Control settings' and enable it again (restart required). The script deliberately does not change this itself.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"uac-off"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="wdigest"></a>
### `wdigest`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** WDigest stores passwords in clear text in memory

**What it means.** With UseLogonCredential=1 any tool that can read memory (e.g. Mimikatz) can read your Windows password in plain text. It is a classic attacker setting.

**What to do.** Set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest\UseLogonCredential to 0 (or delete it) and check the PC for malware.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"wdigest"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="winlogon-shell"></a>
### `winlogon-shell`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** The Windows shell value was changed

**What it means.** HKLM\...\Winlogon\Shell should be exactly "explorer.exe". Anything else is started at every sign-in and is a typical malware persistence trick.

**What to do.** Reset the value to explorer.exe and run a full virus scan (offline scan recommended).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"winlogon-shell"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="winlogon-userinit"></a>
### `winlogon-userinit`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** The Winlogon Userinit value was changed

**What it means.** Userinit should be exactly "C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe,". Extra programs there start at every sign-in with your rights.

**What to do.** Reset the value and run a full virus scan.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"winlogon-userinit"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="defender-sig"></a>
### `defender-sig`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** Virus signatures are … days old

**What it means.** Antivirus scanners only detect known threats. Outdated signatures mean a protection gap against new malware.

**What to do.** The script updates the signatures in the optimization module; alternatively Windows Security > Protection updates.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"defender-sig"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="firewall-wide-open"></a>
### `firewall-wide-open`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … custom firewall rule(s) allow all inbound traffic

**What it means.** A rule with no program, no port and no address restriction switches the firewall off for everything it covers.

**What to do.** Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security > Inbound Rules: delete or restrict these rules.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"firewall-wide-open"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="ntlmv1"></a>
### `ntlmv1`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** Outdated NTLM authentication allowed (LmCompatibilityLevel …)

**What it means.** Values below 3 let this PC send weak LM/NTLMv1 hashes, which can be cracked in minutes.

**What to do.** Set LmCompatibilityLevel to 5 (NTLMv2 only) in the registry or via Local Security Policy, unless a very old device needs it.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"ntlmv1"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="rdp-on"></a>
### `rdp-on`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** Remote Desktop access is turned on

**What it means.** Remote Desktop lets someone on the network sign in to this PC. If the service is reachable from the internet, it is a main entry point for attacks.

**What to do.** If you do not need it: turn it off under Settings > System > Remote Desktop.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"rdp-on"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="restore-off"></a>
### `restore-off`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** System Restore was turned off

**What it means.** Without System Restore, faulty drivers or updates cannot be rolled back via a restore point.

**What to do.** The script turned on System Restore for the system drive.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"restore-off"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="smb1"></a>
### `smb1`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** Outdated network protocol SMB1 is active

**What it means.** SMB1 is a file-sharing protocol over 30 years old with serious security holes (the basis of WannaCry, among others). Only very old devices (old NAS, printers) still need it.

**What to do.** Turn it off unless an old device depends on it: PowerShell (admin) 'Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol …'.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"smb1"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="smb1-feature"></a>
### `smb1-feature`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** The SMB1 Windows feature is installed

**What it means.** Even if the SMB1 server is off, the installed feature keeps the outdated and exploitable SMB1 client/server components on the PC.

**What to do.** Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol (restart required). Old NAS devices may stop working.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"smb1-feature"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="autorun-on"></a>
### `autorun-on`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** AutoRun is enabled for all drive types

**What it means.** Plugging in an infected USB stick can start programs without asking.

**What to do.** Set NoDriveTypeAutoRun to 255 (0xFF) or use Settings > Devices > AutoPlay.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"autorun-on"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="certs-expiring"></a>
### `certs-expiring`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** … computer certificate(s) expired or expire within 30 days

**What it means.** Expired certificates break VPN, Wi-Fi 802.1X, RDP or internal web access.

**What to do.** Renew or remove the certificates you no longer use (certlm.msc).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"certs-expiring"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="defender-cloud"></a>
### `defender-cloud`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Defender cloud-delivered protection is off

**What it means.** Cloud protection lets Defender recognise brand-new malware within minutes instead of waiting for the next signature update.

**What to do.** Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage settings > Cloud-delivered protection: On.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"defender-cloud"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="defender-scan-old"></a>
### `defender-scan-old`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** No virus scan for over 2 weeks

**What it means.** Real-time protection detects a lot, but regular scans also find dormant threats.

**What to do.** The optimization module offers a quick scan.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"defender-scan-old"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="defender-tamper"></a>
### `defender-tamper`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Defender Tamper Protection is off

**What it means.** Tamper Protection stops malware (and scripts) from switching Defender off.

**What to do.** Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage settings > Tamper Protection: On.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"defender-tamper"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="feature"></a>
### `feature-<…>`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Legacy feature '…' is installed

**What it means.** Telnet and TFTP send everything unencrypted and are rarely needed.

**What to do.** Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName …

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"feature*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="psv2"></a>
### `psv2`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Windows PowerShell 2.0 is installed

**What it means.** PowerShell 2.0 has no modern logging or AMSI protection; attackers use it to bypass defences ("downgrade attack").

**What to do.** Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root (restart not needed for most systems).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"psv2"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="shadow-storage"></a>
### `shadow-storage`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** No space is reserved for System Restore

**What it means.** Restore points need reserved disk space (shadow storage). Without it they cannot be kept.

**What to do.** PowerShell (admin): vssadmin Resize ShadowStorage /For=…:SystemDrive /On=…:SystemDrive /MaxSize=5%

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"shadow-storage"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="smartscreen-off"></a>
### `smartscreen-off`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Windows SmartScreen is turned off

**What it means.** SmartScreen warns before you run unknown downloaded programs.

**What to do.** Windows Security > App & browser control > Reputation-based protection: turn it on.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"smartscreen-off"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="bitlocker-off"></a>
### `bitlocker-off`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** The system drive is not encrypted (BitLocker off on …)

**What it means.** If a laptop is lost or stolen, an unencrypted drive can be read by anyone, even without your password.

**What to do.** Windows 10 Pro: Control Panel > BitLocker Drive Encryption. SAVE the recovery key outside the PC. Home: "Device encryption" in Settings > Update & Security if available.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"bitlocker-off"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="defender-pua"></a>
### `defender-pua`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** Protection against potentially unwanted apps is off

**What it means.** This blocks adware and bundled "optimizer" junk.

**What to do.** Windows Security > App & browser control > Reputation-based protection > Potentially unwanted app blocking.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"defender-pua"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="hosts-large"></a>
### `hosts-large`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** The hosts file contains … entries

**What it means.** Large hosts files usually come from ad/tracker blockers. They are harmless but can block legitimate sites.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"hosts-large"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="secureboot-off"></a>
### `secureboot-off`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** Secure Boot is turned off

**What it means.** Secure Boot prevents tampered boot loaders (bootkits) from starting before Windows. When turned off, it is often intentional (dual boot) - but the security benefit is lost.

**What to do.** Can be enabled in the UEFI/BIOS if the PC was installed in UEFI mode. Only change it if you know what you are doing.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"secureboot-off"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Services

<a id="services-disabled"></a>
### `services-disabled`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** … important Windows service(s) were disabled

**What it means.** These services are required for updates, security or system stability. They are often switched off by "optimization tools" and then cause hard-to-explain errors (e.g. update error 0x80070422).

**What to do.** The script reset the services to the Windows default startup type. No further action needed.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"services-disabled"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="services-disabled-failed"></a>
### `services-disabled-failed`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** … disabled service(s) could not be reset

**What it means.** Services are disabled and could not be corrected automatically (e.g. protected by group policy or security software).

**What to do.** Open services.msc, double-click the service and set the startup type back to the default manually; on company computers ask the IT department.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"services-disabled-failed"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="services-error"></a>
### `services-error`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … automatically starting service(s) ended with an error and do not start

**What it means.** A service that should run automatically has crashed or does not start. Consequence: the related function (e.g. driver software, cloud sync, security program) is missing.

**What to do.** Update/reinstall the related software. Details: Event Viewer > Windows Logs > System.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"services-error"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Software

<a id="browser-old"></a>
### `browser-old-<…>`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … has not been updated for … days

**What it means.** Browsers are patched every few weeks; an old build has known, publicly exploitable holes.

**What to do.** Open the browser > About, let it update, and restart it (or run the winget upgrade step).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"browser-old*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="eol-software"></a>
### `eol-software`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … installed program(s) are out of support

**What it means.** Software that no longer gets security fixes is a favourite entry point for attackers (browser plug-ins, Java, old Office/Acrobat).

**What to do.** Uninstall them or replace them with a supported version.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"eol-software"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="office-updates-off"></a>
### `office-updates-off`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** Microsoft Office updates are turned off

**What it means.** Office is a prime target for attackers; without updates known holes stay open.

**What to do.** Any Office app > File > Account > Update Options > Enable Updates.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"office-updates-off"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Stability

<a id="bsod-dumps"></a>
### `bsod-dumps`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** ….Count) blue screen crash dump(s) in the last 30 days

**What it means.** On every blue screen Windows writes a crash dump. It helps to determine the causing driver.

**What to do.** Use the free Microsoft tool WinDbg or NirSoft BlueScreenView to determine the causing driver. The files are located in C:\Windows\Minidump and were deliberately NOT deleted by this script.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"bsod-dumps"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="stability-low"></a>
### `stability-low`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** Reliability index is low (… / 10)

**What it means.** The Reliability Monitor condenses crashes, hangs and failed installs into one score. Below 5 the PC has had repeated problems recently.

**What to do.** Open "View reliability history" (Start menu search) to see which program or update caused the drops.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"stability-low"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Storage

<a id="driverstore-old"></a>
### `driverstore-old`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** … old driver package version(s) in the driver store

**What it means.** Windows keeps previous driver versions for rollback. More than two per driver is rarely useful and wastes space.

**What to do.** The Cleanup module offers to remove all but the newest two versions of each driver (never drivers in use).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"driverstore-old"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="hiberfil-big"></a>
### `hiberfil-big`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** hiberfil.sys occupies …

**What it means.** The hibernation file stores memory content for hibernate and Fast Startup. On a tight system drive it is a quick way to win space.

**What to do.** Admin command prompt: 'powercfg /h /type reduced' (keeps Fast Startup, smaller file) or 'powercfg /h off' (no hibernate, no Fast Startup).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"hiberfil-big"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="leftover"></a>
### `leftover-<…>`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** … occupies …

**What it means.** These folders are created by large Windows updates or upgrade preparations. They allow rolling back to the old version. If ….~BT was created by a Windows 11 preparation, it is unnecessary.

**What to do.** Delete safely via: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > "Previous Windows installation(s)" or Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files. Do not delete manually in Explorer. After deletion, rolling back is no longer possible.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"leftover*"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="recycle-bin"></a>
### `recycle-bin`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** Recycle Bin occupies about …

**What it means.** Files deleted into the Recycle Bin keep occupying storage until it is emptied. The script only empties it with your explicit consent.

**What to do.** Check the Recycle Bin and empty it manually.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"recycle-bin"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="wsl-vhdx"></a>
### `wsl-vhdx`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** WSL virtual disk(s) occupy ….Sum))

**What it means.** WSL distributions store their files in a .vhdx that grows but never shrinks automatically.

**What to do.** Run "wsl --shutdown", then "Optimize-VHD -Path <file> -Mode Full" (Hyper-V module) or diskpart > select vdisk file=... > compact vdisk.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"wsl-vhdx"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## System

<a id="temp-profile"></a>
### `temp-profile`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** You are signed in with a temporary profile

**What it means.** Windows could not load your real profile. Everything saved in this session is lost at sign-out.

**What to do.** Restart. If it recurs, repair the profile registry key (ProfileList) or create a new user account and copy your data.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"temp-profile"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="reboot-pending"></a>
### `reboot-pending`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** A restart is pending

**What it means.** Windows has prepared changes (e.g. updates) that only take effect after a restart. While it is pending, updates and repairs can fail or remain incomplete.

**What to do.** Save your work, restart Windows and then run the script again.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"reboot-pending"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="reboot-required"></a>
### `reboot-required`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** Restart required to complete the maintenance

**What it means.** Updates or repairs were prepared and only take effect after a restart. Until then, security holes may still be open.

**What to do.** Save your work and restart Windows. Then run the script again to check whether everything is clean.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"reboot-required"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="not-activated"></a>
### `not-activated`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** Windows is not activated (…)

**What it means.** Unactivated Windows shows a watermark and blocks personalization; some updates and features can be limited.

**What to do.** Settings > Update & Security > Activation. Use a genuine license key or digital license.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"not-activated"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="print-stuck"></a>
### `print-stuck`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** … print job file(s) are stuck in the spooler queue

**What it means.** Old queue files block printing ("printer offline" / jobs that never finish).

**What to do.** Stop the Print Spooler, delete the queue files, start it again (the script can do this).

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"print-stuck"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="uptime-long"></a>
### `uptime-long`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** The PC has been running for … days without a restart

**What it means.** On Windows 10 with Fast Startup enabled, "Shut down" does not mean a real restart. Memory leaks, hung drivers and unfinished updates accumulate.

**What to do.** Choose 'Restart' (not 'Shut down') once. This is the simplest measure against many strange errors.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"uptime-long"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

## Windows Update

<a id="au-off"></a>
### `au-off`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** Automatic updates are turned off by policy

**What it means.** Windows does not install updates by itself - security holes stay open until someone searches manually.

**What to do.** If this is not intended: gpedit.msc > Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows Update > set 'Configure Automatic Updates' to 'Not configured'.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"au-off"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="os-not-22h2"></a>
### `os-not-22h2`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** Windows 10 is not up to date (version … instead of 22H2)

**What it means.** Windows 10 version 22H2 is the last Windows 10 version. Older versions no longer receive security updates. The update to 22H2 stays Windows 10 - it is NOT Windows 11.

**What to do.** The script's update module offers the feature update to Windows 10 22H2, provided Windows Update makes it available.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"os-not-22h2"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="update-install-error"></a>
### `update-install-error`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** … update(s) could not be installed

**What it means.** At least one update failed. The cause for each update is listed here.

**What to do.** Restart and run the script again. If the error persists, follow the stated solution for each update; for component store errors run the Integrity module.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"update-install-error"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="update-search"></a>
### `update-search`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** The search for Windows updates failed

**What it means.** …

**What to do.** …

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"update-search"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="updates-old"></a>
### `updates-old`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** The last Windows update is … days old

**What it means.** Microsoft publishes security updates monthly. If several are missing, known vulnerabilities are open on this PC.

**What to do.** Install updates now (this module) and pay attention to the error report if errors occur.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"updates-old"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="win11-assistant"></a>
### `win11-assistant`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** The Windows 11 installation assistant is running

**What it means.** This program would upgrade your system to Windows 11.

**What to do.** Terminate the process.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"win11-assistant"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="win11-block-error"></a>
### `win11-block-error`

**Severity:** High · **Title:** Windows 11 block could not be set permanently

**What it means.** The policy that permanently keeps Windows 11 out of Windows Update could not be written. This script never installs Windows 11 anyway; however, Windows Update itself might offer it later.

**What to do.** Run as administrator and check for security software that blocks registry write access.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"win11-block-error"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="update-history-error"></a>
### `update-history-error`

**Severity:** Medium · **Title:** … failed update installation(s) in the last 30 days

**What it means.** Earlier update installations failed. The error codes reveal the cause; the evaluation is below.

**What to do.** The script now tries the updates again and resets the update components if necessary.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"update-history-error"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="updates-deferred"></a>
### `updates-deferred`

**Severity:** Low · **Title:** … update(s) are waiting but were not installed

**What it means.** Installing was skipped because the PC is on battery power or the system drive is nearly full.

**What to do.** Plug in the PC / free up space and run the script again.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"updates-deferred"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="driver-updates"></a>
### `driver-updates`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** … optional driver update(s) available through Windows Update

**What it means.** Windows Update offers drivers that the script deliberately does not install automatically, because wrong drivers can cause problems.

**What to do.** Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update > "View optional updates" and select individual drivers only if needed. It is better to download graphics drivers directly from the manufacturer.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"driver-updates"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="preview-updates"></a>
### `preview-updates`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** … optional preview update(s) not installed

**What it means.** Preview updates (Optional/Preview) are test versions of the next monthly updates and contain bug fixes that are not yet mature. They are not needed for security.

**What to do.** Normally do not install; the contents arrive on the next regular Patch Tuesday.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"preview-updates"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.

<a id="wsus"></a>
### `wsus`

**Severity:** Info · **Title:** Updates come from an internal WSUS server

**What it means.** A policy redirects Windows Update to a company server. Available updates then depend on what IT approves.

Suppress it (if you accept the risk): add `"wsus"` to `SuppressFindings` in the config file.
